bluf: Merkle is dentsu's enterprise customer experience consultancy, selling data, identity, CRM and loyalty work on Adobe, Salesforce and Snowflake platforms from Columbia, MD. The record shows it packaging that work into Adobe products: industry CX solutions in 2026, the Samsung Electronics Europe CRM mandate in 2026-03, a Talon.One loyalty partnership on 2026-09-17 and a Customer Value Hub for travel and hospitality in 2026-09. Horus reads it Favored at 23.2, best placed for KJ4 and most exposed to KJ6. The one thing a rival should know: 16 of its 20 named clients are names only, it publishes no pricing, and dentsu folded the brand in Australia and New Zealand in 2026-05.
doing:
Merkle's positioning line (dentsu's data-led customer experience transformation consultancy uniting identity data, CX platforms, CRM and loyalty, and design) decodes to a marketing systems integrator for enterprise buyers: it builds the customer data layer and the CRM and loyalty programmes that use it. The headline claim, Leader in the IDC MarketScape for Adobe Experience Cloud professional services, 2024-2025, is a platform implementation credential, not a marketing outcome.

The sold mix leads with Data & Measurement (score 3: the Data & Identity line, Merkury, first agency partner on Adobe Mix Modeler) and Email & CRM (score 3: LoyaltyPlus, the Samsung Europe CRM mandate, its own Google ads selling CRM services). Core at score 2: AI Automation / Agents, B2B & ABM (Volvo Trucks, Siemens, VMware) and Web & Product. AI Search / GEO, CRO and Retail Media score 1; every performance media, search and creator line scores 0, and the Performance media family sits at 0 against 3.45 for Data & measurement. Proprietary: Merkury, LoyaltyPlus, Merkle Arc, GenCX, the Customer Value Hub for Travel & Hospitality and a ShopNXT service slug. Partners listed include Adobe, Salesforce, Snowflake and Shopify.

AI posture: enterprise AI scaling and GenCX generative CX technology, AI embedded across data, identity and CRM offers, LinkedIn ads pushing agent ready content.

Moves in date order: 2025-10, dentsu disclosed a breach in which attackers took Merkle data, including staff and client information; 2026, industry specific CX solutions on Adobe Experience Cloud; 2026-03, Samsung Electronics Europe appointed it to transform CRM across 16 European markets; 2026-05, dentsu folded the Australia and New Zealand brand into dentsu and sold the local Salesforce practice to Enduring Ventures; 2026-09-17, a global loyalty partnership with Talon.One; 2026-09, the Customer Value Hub on Adobe CX Enterprise, described in the release as a hospitality native memory layer alongside Adobe Journey Optimizer.

The record lists no pricing model. Conspicuously absent: an employee count, a founding year, jobs or an ATS (jobs count 0), any paid media line, and any SEO line on a 1572 URL site.
clients:
Merkle's client type is enterprise; the verticals listed are Automotive, Retail, CPG & Restaurants, Financial Services, Insurance, Health, High Tech, Media & Entertainment, Nonprofit, Travel & Hospitality and B2B, and the office list spans Europe, Latin America and Asia from a head office in Columbia, MD.

The needs read names 20 clients, 4 observed and 16 names only. Observed: Samsung Electronics Europe came for CRM and owned audiences (press release, 2026-03); Swiss Life for web build and platform (case study, Swiss Life Website Relaunch, 2026-09-08); World Wildlife Fund for brand and creative (case study on chat for brand and audience connection, 2026-09-08); Under Armour for commerce and marketplaces (case study slug, A longstanding partnership drives commerce performance, 2026-09-08). The mix read: web build and brand 0.278 each, CRM 0.25, commerce 0.194.

The 16 names only are Party City, Swisscard, Siemens, Pret A Manger, Volvo Trucks, MINI, Novo Nordisk, Income Insurance, Citizens Access, Compare the Market, AAA Life, Subway, JCPenney, Vodafone, VMware and Allianz. The read codes no need for them, so what they came for is inferred from the sold mix. The case study index also carries Ted Baker, VELUX and Tremco outside the needs count; the deepen pass counted 228 case studies.

Shared clients: Siemens also sits on iprospect and diva-e; Under Armour on iprospect and code-and-theory; Allianz on transmission and webranking; Party City on np-digital; Volvo Trucks on valtech; Compare the Market on neomam-studios; Vodafone on transmission: 7 in all.

What the base needs next, tied to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better): likely, moderate confidence, identity and measurement rebuilds rather than campaign hours, which suits the sold mix; a roughly even chance, low confidence, that the names only accounts are live engagements, since the record describes no work for them.

market:
Horus reads Merkle Favored, tailwind index 23.2, percentile 79, resilience 37.8, the sold mix at 16:37 on the Solar Arc, dusk (Atum), best scenario fit The Walled Oasis at 43/100. Best placed for KJ4, the platforms are absorbing the execution layer (net 0.7, driven by Data & Measurement), and KJ9, measurement gets worse before it gets better (net 0.35, Data & Measurement). Most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out (net -0.36, driven by AI Automation / Agents). Moves: making P7; partial on P1 (no audited AI visibility product) and P6; absent on P2; unknown on P5; P3, P4 and P8 not applicable.

Monsoon reads Onshore wind at 56.3, percentile 51: migration 69.8 against displacement 42.8, so the hours move inside the firm before a client displaces it on price. 48 of the index is the sold mix, Web & Product (12) and Data & Measurement (9) carrying the most movable hours. Shore: 55% South and Southeast Asia, 17% Eastern Europe, 28% Latin America. Observed footprint: hub offices in Argentina, Brazil, Bulgaria, Chile, Colombia and Thailand. No onshore claims listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the book: 16 of the 20 named clients carry no described work, the record lists no pricing model (P5 unknown), and the sold mix is the AI automation and data hours KJ6 removes. A rival who prices on outputs and shows audited work can likely (moderate confidence) contest the names only accounts, starting with the shared ones: Siemens, Under Armour, Allianz, Party City, Volvo Trucks, Compare the Market and Vodafone. Falsifier: case study pages for those accounts dated after 2026-09-28 that describe the work with figures, or a published rate card.

The contradiction to lead with: its LinkedIn ads tell buyers that AI scrapes websites and content must be structured for agents, while its own site has no llms.txt, its AI Search / GEO line scores 1 and P1 is partial; a rival with an audited AI visibility product very likely leads with the number. P2 is absent: feed, schema and entity work around its Adobe and Sitecore builds is unclaimed (likely, moderate confidence).

The 2026-05 Australia and New Zealand fold and the Salesforce practice sale to Enduring Ventures put those clients in transition; the 2025-10 breach and the hub offices in Argentina, Brazil, Bulgaria, Chile, Colombia and Thailand give an onshore, security led pitch something concrete, though unlikely to move enterprise accounts alone.
